figure_caption: Evidence structure of the fixed empirical-game audit. A fixed fitted classifier, explained input, and empirical training background define a probability-scale interventional game over original feature groups, with preprocessing after masking. The studied coalition-regression configuration has six retained repetitions per budget; the measured library comparator is KernelExplainer, not the original independent sampler, which lacks paired final arrays. Top-three repeat agreement, reference fidelity, and efficiency answer different questions; efficiency is imposed by the studied solver. ACSIncome anchors enumerate all 1,024 coalitions and are exact only for the empirical game. German Credit uses two independently seeded 2,048-coalition approximate package anchors; ordinary fidelity averages the two reference-specific qualities. Allocation compares the mean vector of four additional 64-coalition calls with the first retained 256-coalition call, using one common allocation reference: exact for ACSIncome and the mean approximate vector for German Credit. Delta is short-mean quality minus long-call quality. Requested coalition rows, including endpoints, are matched; runtime is not matched. Arrows indicate computational dependencies, not causal validation or sampler superiority. Detailed retained diagnostics are unverified.

panels.title: Fixed empirical-game audit
panels.short_caption: One shared empirical game supports estimator diagnostics, dataset-specific reference anchors, and a neutral four-short versus one-long allocation comparison; no performance ranking is shown.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: one fixed empirical game supports distinct estimator, reference, and budget-allocation questions without implying that any sampler is superior. Draw one connected, wide landscape dependency diagram, not independent mini-panels or a results chart. Use the full-width 21:9 canvas with a narrow input/oracle region at far left, estimator lanes across the upper middle, readouts at upper right, reference anchors across the lower middle, and a compact allocation fork at lower right. Allow sufficient height for a horizontal divider between upper diagnostics and lower reference/allocation content; this divider is only a grouping boundary, not a data edge. Prioritize a readable shared game, the studied-versus-library distinction, explicit exact/approximate anchors, and the 4 x 64 versus 1 x 256 fork. Secondary priority is separation of agreement, fidelity, and efficiency. The original independent sampler is a small peripheral scope note, not a third measured contender. No aesthetics or hue semantics are prescribed. No result magnitudes, plots, rankings, trophies, upward quality arrows, causal arrows, or numeric attribution values. No caption letters.

REGIONS AND STABLE ELEMENT IDS: fixed_cell is a grouping region titled 'Fixed within cell'. Inside it, model_f is a sharp-corner model-artifact box labelled 'Fitted classifier' with symbol '$$f$$', explicitly frozen during explanation, not a trainable node; input_x is a sharp data box labelled 'Explained input' with '$$x$$'; background_b is a cylinder labelled 'Training background' with '$$B$$', a fixed empirical store. Immediately right of these inputs, mask is a rounded process box labelled 'Grouped masking', with the short adjacent annotation mask_note 'Original feature groups'. Below or immediately after mask, prep is a rounded process box labelled 'Fitted preprocessing', explicitly fixed rather than trainable. oracle is a prominent rounded process box labelled 'Background average' with symbol '$$v_{x,B}(S)$$' and adjacent annotation scale_note 'Positive-class probability'. It averages the fitted model outputs across background rows; do not depict averaging the masked feature vectors. A routing junction game_bus, with no text, distributes this oracle to all downstream explanation/reference processes; it is the same game, not different backgrounds or refitting.

The upper estimator group estimators has heading 'Compared estimators'. studied is a rounded process box labelled 'Studied configuration' with two subordinate short lines 'Stratified complement sampling' and 'Efficiency-constrained regression'; its operations are fixed algorithms, not trainable model layers. study_vectors is a compact stack of sharp output-vector cards, labelled '6 repeats / budget', with a shared adjacent budget_note '$$q=64,256$$'; the repeated cards encode different explanation streams, not different fitted models. Do not invent vector entries. library is an equally prominent rounded process box labelled 'KernelExplainer', with the subordinate settings 'Identity link' and 'l1_reg = 0'. library_vector is one sharp output-vector card labelled '1 retained call / budget', with no invented entries. library uses the same two nominal budgets and requests q minus two interior masks, with endpoints accounted for; put this detail in the caption, not a formula on the canvas. original_note is a smaller dashed-outline methodological-scope card labelled 'Original independent sampler' and 'No paired final arrays'; it is a fixed baseline algorithm, not a retained result. Do not connect it to measured readouts, and do not merge it with KernelExplainer.

The upper-right group readouts is titled 'Separate readouts'. agreement is a sharp derived-diagnostic card labelled 'Top-3 repeat agreement', efficiency is a sharp diagnostic card labelled 'Efficiency' with the subordinate noun phrase 'Solver constraint', and fidelity is a sharp diagnostic card labelled 'Reference fidelity' with symbol '$$Q$$'. These are different computed quantities, not probabilities, and have equal visual status. Neither agreement nor efficiency feeds fidelity. study_vectors supplies all three readouts; library_vector supplies only fidelity, since no library repeat series is retained. No diagnostic contains a measured value or a formula.

The lower-middle group anchors is headed 'Reference anchors'. exact_ref is a sharp reference-result card, with a solid outline and an attached small enumeration-process glyph or rounded header, labelled on separate short lines 'ACSIncome', 'Exact enumeration', and '1,024 coalitions'; it denotes the exact Shapley vector for the 10-group finite game. approx_ref is a sharp reference-result card, with a dashed outline and an attached small estimation-process glyph or rounded header, labelled 'German Credit', '2 approximate anchors', and '2 x 2,048 coalitions'; it denotes two independently seeded higher-budget package vectors for the 20-group game. The solid/dashed outline distinction encodes exact versus approximate reference status, not performance. These are dataset alternatives, not two sequential stages and not two anchors for the same dataset. ordinary_policy is a small sharp auxiliary-policy card labelled 'Ordinary fidelity' with two short lines 'ACS: exact anchor' and 'German: mean of qualities'. allocation_policy is a small sharp auxiliary-policy card labelled 'Allocation reference' with symbol '$$r_*$$' and two short lines 'ACS: exact anchor' and 'German: mean vector'. These two policy cards must remain distinct: averaging German reference-specific qualities is not averaging German reference vectors. Do not add another equation or a reference-convergence claim.

The lower-right group allocation is titled 'Equal-coalition allocation'. short_calls is four separate, equally sized rounded process cards with stable IDs short_1, short_2, short_3, short_4, each labelled '64' under the shared group label '4 additional calls'; they represent additional independent streams of the studied configuration, not a subset of study_vectors. long_call is one rounded process card labelled '256' under the shared group label 'First long call'; it represents the first retained long estimate and is not selected for quality. average is a small circular averaging junction containing '$$\oplus$$', named by the adjacent noun phrase 'Mean vector'. Each of its four inbound short-call edges carries '$$1/4$$'; this averaging primitive must not become an equation box. q_short and q_long are equally sized rounded quality-computation processes labelled '$$Q$$', each accepting its own branch vector and the same allocation reference. contrast is a sharp derived-output card labelled 'Allocation contrast' with symbol '$$\Delta$$'; connect q_short and q_long into it with edge labels '+' and '-' respectively, defining short quality minus long quality without printing a raw equation. Along the allocation group bottom, use a neutral bracket joining the two branches with annotation equal_rows '256 coalition rows each' and a second annotation runtime_note 'Runtime not matched'. This is a budget comparison, not a positive or negative measured finding.

COMPLETE EDGE LIST: all ordinary computation/data dependencies below are solid arrowed edges unless explicitly marked dashed. input_x -> mask and background_b -> mask are unlabelled; mask -> prep is unlabelled; prep -> oracle is unlabelled, with model_f -> oracle labelled '$$f$$' as the fixed classifier used on preprocessed masked rows. oracle -> game_bus is unlabelled. game_bus -> studied, game_bus -> library, game_bus -> original_note, game_bus -> exact_ref, and game_bus -> approx_ref are unlabelled solid game-query dependencies. studied -> study_vectors and library -> library_vector are unlabelled solid output edges. study_vectors -> agreement, study_vectors -> efficiency, study_vectors -> fidelity, and library_vector -> fidelity are unlabelled solid diagnostic inputs. exact_ref -> ordinary_policy and approx_ref -> ordinary_policy are dashed unlabelled auxiliary-reference edges; ordinary_policy -> fidelity is dashed and unlabelled. exact_ref -> allocation_policy and approx_ref -> allocation_policy are dashed unlabelled auxiliary-reference edges. From game_bus run a single solid routing trunk into the allocation group and fork to short_1, short_2, short_3, short_4 and long_call, all unlabelled. short_1 -> average, short_2 -> average, short_3 -> average, and short_4 -> average are solid and each labelled '$$1/4$$'. average -> q_short and long_call -> q_long are solid and unlabelled. allocation_policy -> q_short and allocation_policy -> q_long are dashed unlabelled auxiliary-reference inputs, using a shared reference trunk. q_short -> contrast is solid labelled '+'; q_long -> contrast is solid labelled '-'. No other edges, no gradients, and no feedback or training arrows. Dashed means auxiliary reference input; a dashed box border separately marks approximate/unmeasured scope.

SPATIAL RULES: align studied and library in two comparable horizontal lanes, each with its own output card; place the small original_note beneath them without an output lane. Align agreement, fidelity, and efficiency as a compact readout bank at upper right, routing the repeated-vector diagnostic edges independently. Keep exact_ref and approx_ref adjacent in the lower reference band; ordinary_policy lies toward fidelity and allocation_policy toward the allocation fork, so their auxiliary routes remain separate. Use orthogonal connectors, an upper distribution spine for estimator queries and a lower distribution spine for reference/allocation queries, derived from the same game_bus. Do not run connectors through boxes or labels; route reference inputs around the perimeter of the allocation block. Within allocation, put the four small short-call cards above or beside their average junction, and align the long branch in parallel with that mean-vector branch; the quality nodes then merge at contrast. The bracket for equal rows is non-directional. If needed, compress secondary setting text rather than shrinking the core labels or omitting the reference-reduction distinction.

EXACT TEXT BUDGET: only the panel title 'Fixed empirical-game audit'; the region headings 'Fixed within cell', 'Compared estimators', 'Separate readouts', 'Reference anchors', 'Equal-coalition allocation'; the labels and symbols explicitly enumerated above; the unlabelled routing junction; and the specified edge labels '$$f$$', '$$1/4$$', '+', '-'. Each short-call card contains '64' once; long_call contains '256' once; each Q process contains only '$$Q$$'. No sentences, prose explanations, raw multi-term equations, results, further legends, explanatory footnotes, or placeholder images. All elements are native diagram shapes and text; no deferred plots or generated illustrations are needed.
